Pre-question: Thanks for doing the ama, and also thanks for being so active in this community :)

To get things rolling, I'll shoot out a bunch of questions, answer as many as you like. :)

Questions:

1) It seems like numberfire (I assume you work for them) does a lot of analysis based on algorithms (like NEP). How much is the algorithm analysis weighted versus personal opinion?

2) Have you guys ever taken past seasons pre-season information, and tested your algorithms against that to see how it fares on it's own? If so, how did it go?

3) How do you get inter-team news, like a coach talking up/down a player, or how well they are doing in practice?

4) Do you follow all teams? Or is there a team of people following specific teams?

5) Do you have any other favorite fantasy football analysts, or any fantasy football inspirations?

6) Who is your favorite football player ever? (Doesn't have to be active or fantasy related.)

No problem! It's my pleasure being a part of this growing community and I've had a great time so far interacting with all the members and mods here.

Now, on to the questions:

1) It seems like numberfire (I assume you work for them) does a lot of analysis based on algorithms (like NEP). How much is the algorithm analysis weighted versus personal opinion?

In terms of our Net Expected Points (or NEP), the values generated are 100% based on statistics. For a full explanation of NEP, you can check out our glossary here, but long story short: Our algorithm pulls historical data for every single down and distance situation, and identifies the outcomes of these situations in terms of scoring potential. Based on this we then weigh a player's performance on any given play against these historical, expected values. If he makes a play that improves a teams chances of scoring he receives a positive score, and vice-versa if he does the opposite.

What I love about NEP is it tells you how reliable a player has been and it quantifies something that can't be seen in the final boxscore all the time but is something coaches weigh heavily. For example, our algorithm weighs a 3 yard run on 3rd and 2 (which results in a first down and keeps the drive going) much more heavily than a 5 yard run on 3rd and 20 (which results in a punt). The boxscore will say differently, but we all know which run matters more to coaches when it comes to evaluating players and who should/shouldn't get the rock.

When we do our analysis though, we take an approach that combines raw stats, what our eyes tell us, and the NEP scores to evaluate teams, players, and situations.

2) Have you guys ever taken past seasons pre-season information, and tested your algorithms against that to see how it fares on it's own? If so, how did it go?

Not that I know of, but we do have a writer that has expressed interest in looking into this to see how we've done in seasons past. Our nERD scores were pretty spot on though in terms of ranking teams. I believe our top 12 team rankings by nERD ended up being very close to how the playoffs ended, with the Pats and Seahawks 1 and 2.

3) How do you get inter-team news, like a coach talking up/down a player, or how well they are doing in practice?

Twitter. I follow a lot of beat writers (Chris Wesseling has this great list here) as well as guys in the industry such as Chris Mortensen and Adam Schefter.

4) Do you follow all teams? Or is there a team of people following specific teams?

I really try to follow every team and situation rather than restrict myself to a specific niche. I'm always on the lookout for sleepers and undervalued players because I love finding myself a great value, so I try not to limit myself to a team or division since they can come from anywhere (except maybe the Raiders, sorry Oakland).

5) Do you have any other favorite fantasy football analysts, or any fantasy football inspirations?

Oh man, this list could go on and on. Where to begin...

Say what you will about Matthew Berry, but he knows how to engage an audience and is incredibly entertaining. He was really one of the first analysts I started following, way back when he was known as TMR. He's still one of the guys I look up to in terms of his ability to provide analysis in a way that captivates you and tells a compelling story.

The FootballGuys are all awesome, especially Sigmund Bloom, Cecil Lammey, and Matt Waldman. What I admire about them is that these guys clearly know their stuff inside and out, and are thorough and up front with all their opinions and analysis.

I've also interacted with some great people in this industry including Field Yates, who suggested I get in touch with numberFire to really kick off my work with them, Evan Silva who is probably one of the nicest people I've ever interacted with in our exchanges, and the Fantasy Footballers (Andy Holloway, Mike Wright, and Jason Moore) who were gracious enough to invite me onto their Podcast a few weeks back.

Last but not least all the writers at numberFire, especially our Editor-In-Chief JJ Zachariason. These guys have been great to work with and are extremely smart. They also keep me accountable and on my toes and will let me know if my analysis and work is getting lazy so I love them for that too.

6) Who is your favorite football player ever? (Doesn't have to be active or fantasy related.)

Hands down, LaDainian Tomlinson. The dude was electric and a pleasure to watch every Sunday (and on occassion, Mondays). He also powered a lot of my FF teams to championships in the 2000's so I'll always be thankful for that too.

But honestly those aren't the reasons he's my all time favorite player.

I grew up a Chargers fan, and what I will always be grateful to him for is him single-handedly pulling us out of the Ryan Leaf era. He made the Chargers relevant again and a team the national media actually followed.

I wrote this long tribute to him looking back at his career when the Chargers announced he would be inducted into their Hall of Fame if you're interested in giving it a look!
Thanks for the answers, they were all great. My favorite was the LT pick though. :) I'm also a long-time Chargers fan.
